references.text: Moses stretches out his staff over Egypt at the Lord's command, a recurring motif throughout the plagues
Moses stretches out his staff toward the sky to bring hail upon Egypt, following the same pattern of action
The Lord uses a strong east wind to part the sea, using the same Hebrew expression רוּחַ קָדִים (ruach qadim)
The prediction of the locust plague is now fulfilled as the east wind brings the locusts
The Lord again uses wind (a west wind) to remove the locusts, parallel to how the east wind brought them
The psalmist describes how the Lord let an east wind sweep across the sky, referencing God's control over the winds
Joel describes a locust plague that recalls the plague in Egypt
God sends locusts as punishment, echoing the Egyptian plague
Revelation describes locusts coming from smoke, alluding to the locust plague in Egypt
